title: Silas Marner

vibeProfile.oneLine: A bitter miser loses his gold and finds a lost child instead.

summary: A wronged, embittered weaver named Silas Marner withdraws from the world to hoard his gold, until the gold is stolen and a golden-haired orphan child wanders into his cottage and, over the years, back into his heart. George Eliot's shortest novel is a warm moral fable about loss, community and the redeeming power of love. Compact and beautifully told, it is the most approachable of her books and a quietly moving story of a broken man made whole.
whyReadIt: Eliot's shortest and warmest book, a broken miser saved by a lost child. A quietly perfect fable.

funFacts.text: It is often the first George Eliot novel readers meet, thanks to its short length.
